question: In the unchanged two-compartment C-peptide reference with a fully known synthetic 0-10 minute pulse shape, how does an early-only C-peptide window compare with a hypothetical extension when jointly estimating pulse gain and central removal?
scope: Sampling-information stress test only. No FSIGT glucose/insulin model, actual CIT-07 secretion input, transplant calibration, clinical sampling recommendation or human identifiability claim.

sources.kinetics: Polonsky et al. 1986, DOI 10.1172/JCI112308, p. 99 scheme and p. 103 Table I T1D group means, as implemented in BC-003
sources.schedule: CIT-07 protocol version 8 (20 August 2012), section 9.1.2.8, pp. 81-82: FSIGT clock glucose injection at -0.5 min; C-peptide at -10/-5/-1 and 1/2/3/4/5/7/10 min; later G/I blood-draw times are hypothetical C-peptide additions here

observation.noise: Independent Gaussian engineering noise at all postchallenge times. Each seed's full draw is shared between nested designs. Prechallenge samples are omitted because the incremental baseline is stipulated exactly zero; this is a favorable assumption, not an assay model. No negative-value clipping.

analysis.optimizer: scipy least_squares trf in log parameters; residuals divided by fixed engineering SD; max_nfev 200; xtol, ftol and gtol 1e-11
analysis.report: per-design weighted local singular values/condition; 64 paired noisy two-start fits with failures and bound hits retained; median, 90th percentile and maximum absolute relative gain/k3 errors; no empirically calibrated confidence intervals
analysis.comparison: Descriptive paired distribution only; no pass threshold or post-result noise/bound tuning

verification.reference: Generate synthetic truth by segmented BC-003 ODE with DOP853 rtol 1e-11, atol 1e-13 and max_step 0.125; independently fit with BC-003 exact analytical constant-input convolution.
verification.failure_policy: Record failed or incomplete simulations/fits and full planned denominators. Verification failure marks the experiment incomplete; noisy bound hits or large errors remain reported findings. Do not overwrite output.
